Description: <script setup> is the recommended shorthand for Composition API — less boilerplate and better type inference
Do: Use <script setup> in all new SFCs
Don't: Use Options API or verbose setup() return objects
Code Bad: <script> export default { setup() { return { count: ref(0) } } } </script>

Description: ref() wraps primitives in a reactive object and requires .value access — signals intent clearly
Do: Use ref() for strings / numbers / booleans
Don't: Use reactive() for single primitive values
Code Bad: const state = reactive({ name: '' }) // for a single primitive

Description: reactive() returns a deeply reactive proxy — ideal for grouped related state
Do: Use reactive() for related state objects
Don't: Wrap every primitive individually with ref()
Code Bad: const name = ref('') const email = ref('')

Description: computed() memoizes derived values and only re-evaluates when dependencies change
Do: Derive values with computed()
Don't: Recompute values inline in the template

Guideline: Prefer watchEffect over watch when possible
Description: watchEffect() tracks dependencies automatically — less code and harder to miss a dep
Do: Use watchEffect() for side-effects that depend on reactive state
Don't: Manually list every dependency in watch()

Description: Always stop watchers and clear timers/event listeners in onUnmounted or by using the auto-cleanup provided by watchEffect
Do: Return cleanup function from watchEffect / use onUnmounted
Don't: Leave subscriptions active after component teardown

Description: defineProps<T>() provides compile-time type checking without a runtime options object
Do: Use generic syntax: defineProps<{ title: string }>()
Don't: Use untyped string-array props declaration
Code Good: const props = defineProps<{ label: string; count: number }>()

Description: defineEmits<T>() narrows the allowed event contract and improves IDE autocomplete
Do: Use defineEmits with typed signature
Don't: Emit arbitrary string events without declaration

Description: Only expose what external consumers need — keep internal state private by default
Do: Expose a minimal public API via defineExpose()
Don't: Expose all internal refs to parent
Code Bad: defineExpose({ count name form errors }) // over-exposes

Description: Named slots make component APIs explicit; provide meaningful fallback content to aid developer UX
Do: Use named slots with default fallback content
Don't: Use only default slot for multi-section layouts
Code Bad: <slot /> // no fallback and unnamed for complex layouts

Description: Pinia is the official Vue state library — typed stores with devtools support and no mutations boilerplate
Do: Define stores with defineStore()
Don't: Use Vuex or bare reactive objects for cross-component state
Code Good: export const useCounterStore = defineStore('counter' () => { const n = ref(0); return { n } })
Code Bad: export default { state: () => ({ n: 0 }) } // Vuex pattern

Description: The setup() store format mirrors Composition API — reuse composables and feels consistent
Do: Define Pinia stores using setup function syntax
Don't: Use options-style Pinia stores in new code
Code Good: defineStore('cart', () => { const items = ref([]); return { items } })

Description: storeToRefs() preserves reactivity when destructuring state and getters from a Pinia store
Do: Destructure reactive refs via storeToRefs()
Don't: Destructure the store directly (breaks reactivity)

Description: Business logic that mutates store state belongs inside store actions — not in component methods
Do: Put async data-fetching and mutations in actions
Don't: Mutate store state directly from components

Description: Assigning a new object to a reactive() ref breaks reactivity — mutate properties instead
Do: Mutate properties of reactive objects in place
Don't: Replace the whole reactive object with assignment

Description: toRefs() converts reactive object properties into individual refs so they stay reactive after destructuring
Do: Wrap reactive spread with toRefs()
Don't: Destructure reactive() directly
Code Bad: const { name } = form // name is not reactive

Guideline: Use shallowRef for large immutable data
Description: shallowRef() avoids deep reactivity overhead for large data structures that are replaced wholesale
Do: Use shallowRef() for big arrays/objects replaced atomically
Don't: Use ref() for large datasets you replace frequently
Code Bad: const rows = ref(bigDataArray) // deep observe overhead

Guideline: Use v-memo for expensive list items
Description: v-memo caches a subtree until a dependency array changes — prevents unnecessary re-renders in large lists
Do: Add v-memo to heavy list row components
Don't: Skip v-memo and rely solely on key-based diffing for expensive rows

Description: defineAsyncComponent() splits heavy components into separate chunks — reduces initial bundle size
Do: Wrap page-level or modal components with defineAsyncComponent()
Don't: Import all components statically at the top

Description: <KeepAlive> caches component state across route changes — avoids expensive re-initialization
Do: Wrap tab panels or route views with <KeepAlive>
Don't: Mount/unmount expensive components on every route change

Description: Composition API equivalents of this.$router/$route — required inside <script setup>
Do: Call useRouter() / useRoute() inside setup
Don't: Access $router / $route in <script setup> via template refs
Code Good: const router = useRouter(); const route = useRoute()

Description: Dynamic imports make each route a separate chunk — improves TTFB for large SPAs
Do: Use () => import() for all route components
Don't: Import all page components statically in router.ts

Description: beforeEach() guards enforce authentication and redirect unauthenticated users before rendering
Do: Add a global router.beforeEach() auth guard
Don't: Check auth state inside the component mounted hook

Guideline: Prefer named routes over path strings
Description: Named routes decouple navigation from URL structure — refactoring paths won't break router.push calls
Do: Use name property in route definitions and router.push
Don't: Hard-code path strings in router.push() calls

Description: defineModel() (Vue 3.4+) simplifies two-way binding in child components with a single macro
Do: Use defineModel() for custom input components
Don't: Manually wire :modelValue prop + emit('update:modelValue')

Description: VeeValidate integrates Zod schemas for declarative type-safe form validation — no boilerplate error state
Do: Use useForm() with zodResolver() for validation
Don't: Write manual validation logic and track errors in local refs
Code Good: const { handleSubmit } = useForm({ validationSchema: toTypedSchema(z.object({ email: z.string().email() })) })

Guideline: Use semantic HTML elements in templates
Description: Semantic elements convey meaning to assistive technologies without extra ARIA — prefer them over generic divs
Do: Use <button> <nav> <main> <article> <section> etc
Don't: Use <div> with click handlers for interactive elements

Description: Use :aria-* bindings to keep ARIA state in sync with component state — avoids stale accessibility metadata
Do: Bind aria-expanded / aria-disabled / aria-label dynamically
Don't: Use static aria attributes for dynamic state
